title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
authors: T. Brown, B. Mann, N. Ryder, et al. (31 authors)
before: Adapting a pretrained model to a task meant gradient updates and labelled examples.
problem: Fine-tuning per task is slow, needs data, and produces a different model each time.
breakthrough: At 175B parameters, the model learns a task from examples placed in the prompt, with no weight updates at all.
why: In-context learning is the behaviour that made prompting an interface and an API business possible.
next: InstructGPT aligned it, and ChatGPT put it in front of the public.
inherits: Few-shot prompting, and the expectation that one model serves every task.
